_readme: Per-model price table for turning benchmark token usage into dollars.
Prices are USD per 1 MILLION tokens, split input (prompt) / output (completion),
because the models in the campaign differ in price by more than 15x and a
token count alone hides that. Edited by hand; consumed by
experiments/scripts/cost_summary.py at summarize time (never at run time),
so correcting a rate later only requires re-running the summarizer.
VERIFIED 2026-08-06 against the Azure retail price API
(https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices, serviceName 'Foundry Models',
priceType 'Consumption', paged in full). Each entry names the exact meter.
All four campaign deployments on account foundary-tzuc06 (rg-tzuc06,
germanywestcentral) are GlobalStandard, so the GLOBAL meters apply - not
the Data Zone ('DZ') variants, which run 5-10% higher. Confirmed with
`az cognitiveservices account deployment list`.
Rates below are UNCACHED input. Every model also has a cached-input meter at
roughly a tenth of the input rate, recorded as cached_input_usd_per_1m for
reference; cost_summary.py does not use it yet because the runtime does not
record how many prompt tokens were served from cache (usage carries only
prompt_tokens / completion_tokens). Until it does, computed dollars are an
UPPER BOUND. Token counts are unaffected by caching either way, which is why
tokens remain the benchmark's primary, hardware-independent metric.
gpt-5.6-sol note: the ShortCo (short-context) tier is priced here. The
LongCo tier is 2x input / 1.5x output ($10.00 / $45.00) and would apply only
if a single request exceeded the long-context threshold; measured per-call
prompts in the n=1 pilot averaged ~3-6k tokens, far inside ShortCo.
